dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Systematic upfront orientation: lists workspace, reads root Cargo.toml, surveys every crate's src+test files, reads all stubs and all crate Cargo.tomls, counts tests per crate — establishing the contract surface and dependency order (common→storage→api-server).

Deep mining of tests/stubs to reconstruct core type contracts (ObjectMeta/TypeMeta fields, OwnerReference shape, JSON field-name assertions, enum variants), including writing a generator that infers struct fields from test literals.

Per-crate: reads each crate's specific test files and Cargo.toml before implementing (auth, protobuf, admission, webhook, api-server symbol surface), showing consistent test-first orientation across the whole arc.

Zero accesses to /opt/k8s-reference anywhere — the mounted v1.35 upstream 'source of truth' is never consulted; all contract inference is fixture-derived, the approach the task warns the hidden conformance suite penalizes.
Long iterative add-field / fix-compile-error grind reflects contracts reconstructed only from test literals rather than the reference, causing repeated correction rather than a source-of-truth model.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent thoroughly and systematically mines the tests, stubs, and Cargo manifests and clearly understands the cross-crate dependency graph — well beyond anchor 3's 'skims one crate's tests.' But it never once consults the mounted /opt/k8s-reference upstream tree, instead inferring contracts purely from test-file literals via a generator, i.e. exactly the fixture-fitting the dimension flags as dangerous. Anchor 5 explicitly requires consulting the reference for tested behaviors, which the agent does not do, so it lands at 4: strong three-source (tests/stubs/manifests) orientation but with the reference — the emphasized source of truth — entirely absent.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: After surveying test counts and an initial TodoWrite, agent fully implements+tests common crate first (ending 'Summary of common test results'), then moves to storage — leaf-first ordering with per-crate done-check.
api-server decomposed into sub-milestones: lib → storage wiring → handlers (finalizers/filtering/table) → admission → webhook → spdy/patch/response, matching anchor-8 intra-crate decomposition.
Ordered progression common→storage→api-server→controller-manager→scheduler→kubectl with aggregate pass-count done-checks per crate (controller-manager and api-server count aggregation).
Repeated regression re-runs of common/storage/api-server after downstream edits — gating each layer on prior layers staying green.

Common crate was a large reactive compiler-error-driven grind through generated.rs (one struct at a time), not a pre-decomposed set of crisp sub-units — falls short of anchor-8/10 explicit per-unit criteria.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it follows the leaf-to-root DAG order with per-crate compile+test done-checks, decomposes the large api-server crate into wiring/handlers/admission/webhook sub-milestones, and gates layers by re-running upstream tests after downstream changes (regression checks). It stops short of anchor 8/10 because the biggest crate (common) was tackled as a reactive, undifferentiated error-chasing push rather than pre-planned crisp units, and there is no evidence of dynamic re-sequencing or early isolation of high-risk crates. This places observed behavior at a 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Tight per-crate verify loops early: build common, run common tests, recount, fix — establishing a build→targeted-test cadence rather than deferring verification.
Systematic triage of failure clusters: compiles each test target individually, collects all errors, and repeatedly 'summarizes field errors' to group failures — beyond a plain green-suite bar.
Cross-crate regression checks run after each milestone fix (api-server/controller-manager, ephemeral/init, EnvVar/VolumeMount) to confirm changes don't break already-passing crates.
Aggregates exact pass/fail counts per crate and workspace-wide, and reconciles counted test functions against the ~1,390 target — precise horizon tracking feeding verification.

No evidence anywhere of booting the all-in-one binary, HTTP/JSON conformance checks, or independent semantic verification against the /opt/k8s-reference upstream tree; verification is entirely driven by making provided fixtures compile/pass.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent runs a rigorous, tight build→targeted-crate-test→regression→workspace loop with precise pass/fail-count tracking and systematic failure-cluster triage — clearly stronger than anchor 5's 'green provided suite as the bar with periodic workspace runs.' However, the defining addition of anchor 8 — deliberately reasoning about hidden-conformance behavior by booting the all-in-one binary or checking HTTP/JSON semantics, plus anchor 10's independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard against over-fitting — is entirely absent; the whole approach is fixture-fitting. This lands it at 6: above 5 for the count-tracking and triage discipline, well short of 8 for the missing conformance/semantic verification. Confidence is medium because the log exposes only tool-call titles, so unseen prose reasoning about conformance cannot be fully ruled out, though the complete lack of any binary-boot/HTTP action is strong signal.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Repeatedly measured full test scope up front ('Accurate test counts per crate', 'Definitive test count', 'Confirm total available test functions'), establishing the ~1,390-test horizon before implementing.

Maintained a running tally of remaining compile errors and which test targets fail ('Count total errors and codes', 'Recount api-server test errors', 'List failing test targets', 'Compile each test target individually', 'Recheck remaining failing targets') — a concrete updated ledger of remaining work.

Ran explicit regression checks on already-green crates (api-server, controller-manager) after editing shared types for scheduler/kubelet, and polled those outputs — directly watching for regressions in previously-passing crates after downstream edits (the level-8 hallmark).

End-game aggregate accounting: 'aggregate controller-manager counts', 'aggregate api-server counts', 'Aggregate test pass/fail counts', 'Per-package test counts', counting test functions and ignored tests across the workspace.

Recurring TodoWrite updates tracked crate-level milestones across the whole trajectory, though the middle common-crate grind was tracked mainly by error-count reduction rather than reprioritization by largest verified gain.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent measured the full test horizon up front, kept continuously-updated tallies of remaining compile errors and failing test targets, ran deliberate regression checks on previously-green crates after downstream type edits, and produced per-package pass/fail aggregates at the end — squarely matching the level-8 anchor (concrete updated ledger + regression watching). It does not reach 10: there is no evidence of explicitly naming circular/thrashing states or reprioritizing by where the largest verified gains remain, and the long common-crate grind was monitored via error counts rather than a forward-progress-vs-churn distinction.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Revised its auto-generation approach multiple times (string/comment-aware extractor, improved classifier, type/parent_ref patch) when the generator produced wrong struct fields — abandoning the initial extraction logic rather than hand-patching each output.

Dominant loop: compile test → read failing test literal → inspect struct → edit generated.rs → rebuild. Consistently updates the implementation when a test reveals a wrong field/signature (anchor-5), but largely local patch-the-error fixes over hundreds of cycles.

Genuine structural reworks: extracted DRA types into a new dra.rs module after detecting cross-usage, extracted endpointslice.rs, and re-exported LabelSelector via mod.rs — recognizing structural/contract problems, not just typos.

After changing shared common types for scheduler/kubelet, re-ran api-server and controller-manager tests as regression checks — revising the model and re-verifying affected downstream crates (higher-order adaptation signal).
Semantic corrections triggered by test failures (storage creation_timestamp on create; Service cluster_ip), converting failing-test evidence into implementation fixes.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's behavior sits solidly at anchor 5 (consistently updates the implementation and nearby work when a test falsifies a signature/field/semantic) and reaches partway into anchor 8 via several genuine structural reworks (generator rewrite, DRA/endpointslice module extractions) and downstream regression re-verification after shared-crate changes. It never repeats a failing approach unchanged. But most of the arc is local per-type field patching rather than backing out a whole falsified design, and there's no clear crate-reordering-when-blocked, so it falls short of a strong 8. Net: 6 (limited by a condensed log lacking prose, hence medium confidence).

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
